Cash Flow Statement: Indirect Method, Format and Worked Example

A company can show a profit and still run out of cash. The cash flow statement shows where cash actually came from and went, split across three activities. Under Ind AS 7 and AS 3, most companies prepare it by the indirect method.

2 min readFor MBA, BBA and BBMUpdated 2 November 2026

The three activities

ActivityIncludesHealthy sign
OperatingCash from running the businessPositive, and close to profit
InvestingBuying and selling assets and investmentsUsually negative in a growing firm
FinancingBorrowing, repaying, issuing shares, paying dividendsDepends on the stage of the business

Direct and indirect methods

The direct method lists actual cash received and paid. The indirect method starts from profit before tax and adjusts it for non-cash items and changes in working capital. Both give the same answer, but the indirect method is what most companies use, as it shows why profit and cash differ.

A worked example

Sunrise Traders Ltd, using the same figures as our balance sheet and profit and loss guides (₹ lakh).

Particulars₹ lakh
Profit before tax160
Add: depreciation (non-cash)50
Add: interest (shown under financing)40
Less: increase in receivables(20)
Less: increase in inventory(10)
Add: increase in payables15
Less: tax paid(40)
A. Cash from operating activities195
Purchase of fixed assets(120)
B. Cash from investing activities(120)
New borrowings20
Interest paid(40)
Dividend paid(30)
C. Cash from financing activities(50)
Net increase in cash (A + B + C)25
Opening cash55
Closing cash (matches the balance sheet)80

The rules for adjustments

  • Add back non-cash expenses, such as depreciation and amortisation.
  • An increase in a current asset uses cash, so subtract it. A decrease releases cash, so add it.
  • An increase in a current liability saves cash, so add it. A decrease uses cash, so subtract it.
  • Remove investing and financing items, such as interest paid or profit on selling an asset, and show them under their own headings.

Free cash flow

Free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditure = ₹195 lakh − ₹120 lakh = ₹75 lakh.

This is the cash available to repay debt, pay dividends or grow further. It is also the basis of valuing a company by discounted cash flow.

How to read the pattern

OperatingInvestingFinancingLikely meaning
+−−A mature firm, funding itself and repaying debt or paying dividends
+−+A growing firm, adding outside money to its own
−−+A young or struggling firm, relying on outside money
−++ or −Possible distress, selling assets to stay afloat

Exam and interview questions

Why is depreciation added back in the indirect method?

It reduces profit but no cash leaves the business in that period, so it is added back to arrive at cash.

Under which activity is interest paid shown?

For non-financial companies, generally under financing activities. Interest received and dividends received are generally under investing activities.

Can a profitable company go bankrupt?

Yes. If receivables and inventory absorb its cash, it may be unable to pay what is due, even while it reports profits.
